record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of microwave heating
record.context_brief: Asymptotic convergence to the harmonic stationary set M
record.original_question: Consider the nonlinear microwave-heating initial-boundary value problem that couples Maxwell's equations for the electric and magnetic fields E(x,t), H(x,t) with a heat equation for the temperature θ(x,t) on a bounded simply connected domain Ω, where the electrical conductivity σ(θ) and the microwave energy absorption q(θ) both depend on θ. Assume σ(θ) > q(θ) for every temperature θ. Let M be the set of stationary data with E_0(x)=0 and H_0(x)=∇φ(x), where φ is harmonic in Ω. Must every regular solution satisfy lim_{t→∞} dist((E(t), H(t), θ(t)), M) = 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded, simply connected domain with smooth boundary. Consider the coupled microwave-heating initial-boundary value problem for the electric field $E(x,t)$, magnetic field $H(x,t)$, and temperature $\theta(x,t)$ governed by Maxwell's equations
$$\varepsilon\, \partial_t E = \nabla \times H - \sigma(\theta)\, E, \qquad \mu\, \partial_t H = -\nabla \times E,$$
together with the heat equation
$$c\, \partial_t \theta - \nabla\cdot(k\nabla \theta) = q(\theta)\, |E|^2,$$
in $\Omega \times (0,\infty)$, supplemented with the perfect-conductor boundary condition $E\times\nu = 0$ on $\partial\Omega$ and a homogeneous boundary condition for $\theta$ (e.g. $\theta = 0$ or $\partial_\nu\theta = 0$). Here the temperature-dependent electrical conductivity $\sigma(\theta)$ and microwave energy absorption coefficient $q(\theta)$ are smooth, positive functions satisfying
$$\sigma(\theta) > q(\theta) \quad \text{for all } \theta \in \mathbb{R}.$$
Define the set of stationary data
$$M = \{(E_0, H_0, \theta_0) : E_0 \equiv 0,\ H_0 = \nabla\varphi \text{ for some } \varphi \text{ harmonic in } \Omega,\ \theta_0 \text{ stationary}\}.$$
Question: Does every regular (smooth, global) solution $(E,H,\theta)$ of the above system satisfy
$$\lim_{t \to \infty} \mathrm{dist}\bigl((E(\cdot,t), H(\cdot,t), \theta(\cdot,t)),\ M\bigr) = 0\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: The question is stated as an open problem in a published list of open problems on microwave heating (J. Elliptic Parabol. Equ., 2022). A web search did not reveal any subsequent paper proving the asymptotic convergence to the harmonic stationary set M under the hypothesis σ(θ) > q(θ). Related works address regularity and well-posedness of Maxwell–heat couplings but not this asymptotic question, so the problem appears to remain open.
